claim: FineWeb is approximately 15 trillion GPT-2 tokens of Common Crawl data, produced from roughly 36 trillion tokens of raw extracted text before filtering.
stance_target: The size of the web-data pool the repo's 9B-token mix draws from
scope_conditions: FineWeb v1, Common Crawl, GPT-2 tokenizer
quoted_support: we obtained roughly 36 trillion tokens of data when tokenized with the GPT-2 [tokenizer]... FineWeb is approximately 15 trillion tokens.

claim: The FineWeb ablation protocol uses 1.71B-parameter Llama-architecture models at sequence length 2048 with a global batch of ~2 million tokens, trained on ~28B tokens for filtering ablations and 350B tokens for dedup ablations.
stance_target: The repo's claim that a ~1B-trainable model at 1M-token global batches is a legitimate experimental configuration — the published reference point is 1.71B at ~2M tokens
scope_conditions: FineWeb data ablation experiments, nanotron framework, GPT-2 tokenizer
quoted_support: Data ablation models all had 1.71B parameters (including embeddings), used the Llama architecture with a sequence length of 2048, a global batch size of ~2 million tokens, and the GPT2 tokenizer. Filtering ablations were trained on ~28 billion tokens (roughly the Chinchilla-optimal training size for this model size), while some deduplication ablations ... were conducted on 350 billion tokens.

claim: The FineWeb study trained over 70 ablation models for an estimated total of 80,000 H100 GPU hours, which is the compute cost of establishing a data pipeline empirically.
stance_target: The repo's claim that data-pipeline decisions are expensive to validate and must be budgeted as experiments in their own right
quoted_support: In total, we trained over 70 models on our internal cluster, for an estimated total of 80,000 H100 GPU hours.

claim: FineWeb-Edu's educational classifier reached F1 82% at threshold 3 on a held-out validation set, and applying it to the 15T-token FineWeb required 6,000 H100 GPU hours.
stance_target: Whether the repo can reproduce educational filtering locally, and at what accelerator cost
scope_conditions: FineWeb-Edu classifier, Llama3-70B-Instruct annotations, 500k scored CC-MAIN-2024-10 pages
quoted_support: With a threshold of 3, the model achieved an F1 score of 82% on the validation set, indicating strong performance in distinguishing high-quality educational content. Applying the classifier to the 15 trillion tokens of FineWeb required 6,000 H100 GPU hours.

claim: FineWeb's MinHash deduplication uses 112 hash functions arranged into 14 bands of 8 hashes, with union-find over connected components so that transitive duplicate chains are collapsed.
stance_target: The CPU cost and determinism characteristics of the dedup stage in the repo's data pipeline
quoted_support: we computed MinHashes using 112 hash functions in total ... documents with the same 8 MinHashes in any bucket are considered duplicates of each other. We then perform a ... [union-find so that] if A and C are duplicates and B and C are duplicates, even if A and B do not have 8 matching MinHashes in [the same bucket].

claim: FineWeb's ablation protocol trains two models per data version using different random subsets and different initialisation seeds, then averages scores, specifically to control for subset-selection noise.
stance_target: The repo's data-pipeline determinism and acceptance-criteria claims — the published standard is two seeds per comparison
quoted_support: To minimize the impact of random data subset selection on evaluation scores, we trained two models for each dataset version, each using a different but equal-sized random subset of the full data and a different initialization seed, and then compared average scores.

claim: FineWeb's heuristic quality filters were tuned by taking the lower tail of each metric's histogram as the threshold, yielding 16 candidate metric-threshold pairs rather than hand-picked cutoffs.
stance_target: Whether a small run needs to re-derive filtering thresholds or can inherit published ones
quoted_support: we empirically chose thresholds that would target sections of the histogram where the lower quality ... Following this process for all metrics yielded 16 candidate metric-threshold pairs.

claim: Trafilatura extraction from WARC files outperforms using Common Crawl's pre-extracted WET text in the FineWeb ablations, so text-extraction choice is a measurable quality variable.
stance_target: Whether the repo's data pipeline should re-extract from WARC rather than consume WET
quoted_support: text extraction is relatively costly, but its effects are felt on model performance: Fig. 1 shows the performance of ablation models trained on either trafilatura applied to WARC data or WET data.

claim: FineWeb applies a fastText language classifier retaining only English text with a score of at least 0.65, and that threshold is visible in the released dataset's language_score field.
stance_target: Reproducibility of the language-filtering step in a local pipeline
quoted_support: we applied a fastText language classifier to keep only English text with a score >= 0.65.

claim: FineWeb-Edu outperforms FineWeb and all other openly accessible web datasets on educational benchmarks including MMLU, ARC and OpenBookQA.
stance_target: The repo's choice of FineWeb-Edu as the web component of its 9B-token mix
scope_conditions: FineWeb-Edu ablation models, 350B tokens, lighteval benchmarks
quoted_support: FineWeb-Edu is specifically optimized for educational content and outperforms all openly accessible web-based [datasets].
